sources.title: The UAE government portal (u.ae), Public holidays: Union List of holidays (updated 2 July 2026)
sources.said: Following is the list of public holidays applicable to both, public and private sectors. Gregorian New Year - 1 January; Eid Al Fitr* - from 1 to 3 Shawwal (4 days)**; Arafah Day* - 9 Thu Al Hijjah; Eid Al Adha* (Feast of Sacrifice) - From 10 to 12 Thu Al Hijjah (3 days); Hijri New Year* (Islamic New Year) - 1 Muharram; Prophet Mohammed's birthday* - 12 Rabi’ Awwal; National Day - 2 and 3 December (2 days). *Islamic holidays are determined according to moon sighting. **If the month of Ramadan lasts 30 days, day 30 shall be deemed as an official holiday for Eid Al Fitr. Note: According to Article 3 of Cabinet Resolution No. 27 of 2024 Concerning the Public Holidays in the State, the Public Holiday cannot be transferred to another day in the event it coincides with another public holiday or falls on the weekend.

sources.title: Gulf News, UAE announces Eid Al Fitr 2026 holiday (the Federal Authority for Government Human Resources; fahr.gov.ae resets the connection, 2026-10-27)
sources.said: all federal ministries, institutions, and public sector entities will be on holiday from March 19 to 22

sources.title: Khaleej Times, UAE confirms Eid Al Adha 2026 holidays for private sector employees (the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation)
sources.said: Private sector employees in the UAE will receive a four-day paid holiday for Eid Al Adha 2026. ... the holiday will be observed from Tuesday, May 26, to Friday, May 29, 2026.

sources.title: Aletihad, UAE announces Hijri New Year holiday on June 15 (3 June 2026; the Federal Authority for Government Human Resources and the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation)
sources.said: Monday, 15 June 2026, will be an official holiday for federal government entities and private sector establishments

sources.title: Gulf News, UAE declares public holiday for Prophet’s birthday (the UAE Government Media Office)
sources.said: The UAE Government Media Office announced that Friday, August 28, 2026, will be a paid public holiday for employees in the federal government and private sector to mark the Prophet Muhammad's birthday (Mawlid Al Nabawi).
